name: Sindang
confidence_why: The only description of Sindang, Arifin et al. 1996, says stress is not contrastive and can be moved within a word without changing meaning but never says where it normally falls, and McDowell and Anderbeck 2020 do not discuss stress at all, so no placement or stress type can be given for this language.

catalog_locator: Bab III Fonologi, sec. 3.7 'Ciri Suprasegmental', p. 47
catalog_quote: Dalam bahasa Sindang ciri suprasegmental yang bersifat fonemis adalah intonasi atau lagu kalimat. Mari kita perhatikan kalimat (1) dan (2) berikut. (1) Yë bedu kawin. 'Dia sudah kawin.' (2) Yë bedu kawin? 'Dia sudah kawin?' Kalimat (1) yang diucapkan dengan lagu datar berisi informasi bahwa seseorang (yang dirujuk) sudah kawin, sedangkan kalimat (2) yang diucapkan dengan lagu yang agak meninggi pada bagian akhir bermakna menginginkan suatu informasi atau dapat pula menyatakan makna keraguan. Adapun tekanan dalam bahasa Sindang tidak bersifat fonemis. Walaupun tekanan dipidah-pindahkan posisinya pada suatu kata atau walaupun diubah-ubah letak tekanan pada suatu kalimat, maknanya tidak berubah. Biarpun demikian, bila tekanan itu diletakkan pada posisi yang tidak lazim, kata atau kalimat terasa lucu bagi penutur asli bahasa Sindang. Demikian pula unsur tempo (jangka) dalam bahasa Sindang tidak bersifat fonemis. Artinya, panjang atau pendek tempo pengucapan suatu kata atau kalimat tidak membedakan arti.

new_statements.translation: In Sindang the suprasegmental feature that is phonemic is intonation, or sentence melody. [...] As for stress, in Sindang it is not phonemic. Even if the stress is moved from one position to another within a word, or the placement of stress within a sentence is varied, the meaning does not change. Even so, if the stress is put in an unusual position, the word or sentence sounds funny to native speakers of Sindang.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is stated to be non-contrastive: shifting it changes no meanings. The authors imply there is a customary ('lazim') stress position (deviation sounds odd) but never say where it is; only sentence intonation is treated as distinctive. No placement rule can be extracted from this source.
new_statements.exceptions: None; tempo/length (sec. 3.7, same page) likewise stated to be non-phonemic.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement covers both the word ('pada suatu kata') and the sentence ('pada suatu kalimat'); it is a phonemic-status statement, not a phonetic placement description. Data from 'bahasa Sindang' (= Col/Cul/Saling) of Musi Rawas, Rejang Lebong and Lahat, corpus drawn from one unspecified 'original' geographic dialect.
new_statements.identity_note: sind1280 is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for the retired ISO code [sdi] 'Sindang Kelingi', merged in 2008 into Col [liw] (Glottolog coll1240, Malayic, UPPER MUSI cluster per McDowell & Anderbeck 2020). Glottolog files all Sindang descriptions under coll1240. The quoted source, Arifin et al. 1996, describes 'bahasa Sindang' (also called Saling or Cul = Col) as spoken along the Kelingi and Beliti rivers in Musi Rawas (Sumatera Selatan), Padang Ulak Tanding in Rejang Lebong (Bengkulu) and Tebing Tinggi in Lahat, explicitly including the Sindang Kelingi and Sindang Kelingi Ilir areas (sec. 2.1, pp. 6-7); the corpus was taken from one unspecified 'original' geographic dialect. Any catalog entry therefore belongs under coll1240 (Col), with sind1280 as an alias; coll1240 is itself a separate target in our source list with no copies we hold, and the three PDFs saved here serve it directly.

tone_statements.citation: Arifin, Siti Salamah; Tarmizi Abubakar; Hj. Kusmiarti; Hairuddin; Wowo Ario Sungkowo. 1996. Fonologi dan Morfologi Bahasa Sindang. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. ISBN 979-459-675-2.
tone_statements.quote: Samsuri (1983: 135) menjelaskan bahwa peranan bunyi-bunyi prosodi, yaitu tekanan, nada, panjang, danjeda, tidak boleh dilupakan. [...] Oleh sebab itu, penelitian ini juga berusaha menemukan fonem-fonem supraseg­mental, di samping fonem-fonem segmental. [...] 3.7 Ciri Suprasegmental. Dalam bahasa Sindang ciri suprasegmental yang bersifat fonemis adalah intonasi atau lagu kalimat. [...] Adapun tekanan dalam bahasa Sindang tidak bersifat fonemis. [...] Demikian pula unsur tempo Uangka) dalam bahasa Sindang tidak bersifat fon emis. Artinya, panjang atau pendek tempo pengucapan suatu kata atau kalimat tidal< membedakan arti.
tone_statements.translation: Samsuri (1983: 135) explains that the role of the prosodic sounds, namely stress, pitch (tone), length and juncture, must not be forgotten. [...] Therefore this study also tries to find the suprasegmental phonemes, besides the segmental phonemes. [...] 3.7 Suprasegmental features. In Sindang the suprasegmental feature that is phonemic is intonation, or sentence melody. [...] As for stress, in Sindang it is not phonemic. [...] Likewise the element of tempo (length) in Sindang is not phonemic; that is, a long or short tempo in pronouncing a word or sentence does not distinguish meaning. ('Uangka)', 'fon emis', 'tidal<' are the text layer's renderings of '(jangka)', 'fonemis', 'tidak'.)
tone_statements.locator: Bab I p. 3 and Bab III Fonologi, section 3.7 'Ciri Suprasegmental', p. 47

sources.note: Sec. 3.7 'Ciri Suprasegmental', printed p. 47 (p. 64): only sentence intonation is phonemic; stress (tekanan) is not phonemic -- it can be shifted within a word or sentence without changing meaning, though an unusual position 'sounds funny' to native speakers. No statement of where stress normally falls; transcriptions carry no stress marks. Sec. 2.1-2.2 (pp. 6-8) define the Sindang area incl. Sindang Kelingi Ilir, Sindang Beliti, Sindang Kelingi (Padang Ulak Tanding, Rejang Lebong) and Saling; language also called Saling or Cul.

tone.says: The introduction (p. 3) says the study, following Samsuri 1983, also looked for suprasegmental phonemes among stress, pitch (nada), length and juncture; the result in section 3.7 (p. 47) is that the only phonemic suprasegmental feature of Sindang is sentence intonation (statement vs question melody); stress is not phonemic (moving it changes no meaning, only sounds odd) and tempo/length is not phonemic. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. 178 pp. hdl:10524/52473 (downloaded from CORE mirrorhttps://core.ac.uk/download/361383093.pdf;eVols bitstream could not be reached by automated download)
sources.note: Silent: the word 'stress' does not occur anywhere; ch. 5 'Phonological and morphological innovations' (pp. 56-103) is entirely segmental (*h, *s, *r, nasal deletion, high-vowel lowering, final *-a, diphthongs, *a>e, schwa, suffixes). Identity: treats Col [liw, formerly liw+sdi] as a member of the UPPER MUSI cluster of MUSI; Sindang Kelingi is a Col subdialect (not to be confused with Kelingi, a Musi Proper dialect).

sources.citation: Anderbeck, Karl (submitter). 2007. ISO 639-3 change request 2007-196: merge [sdi] Sindang Kelingi into [liw], rename Lembak to Col. SIL International / ISO 639-3 RA. Effective 2008-01-14.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology or stress. Gives language identity (Col = Sindang = Lembak; dialects Sindang Kelingi Ilir, Sindang Kelingi, Sindang Beliti, Saling, plus Lembak Delapan near Bengkulu city), survey dates 2005-2007, and a bibliography naming Arifin et al. 1996, Arifin et al. 1997, McDowell (forthcoming) South Sumatran Survey Report, and Aliana et al. 1984 (Belide dialek Lembak, a Musi lect, not Col).
